profile.entities: Viceroy Hotels Limited; Marriott Executive Apartments Hyderabad; Courtyard by Marriott Hyderabad; Marriott Hotel Hyderabad
profile.subseg: Luxury Hotels; Extended Stay Apartments; MICE & Banqueting
profile.themes: Asset Consolidation; Phased Renovation Upside; Debt-Funded Expansion; Supply Scarcity in Hyderabad

bull_bear.body: Priority 1: Complete asset enhancement (renovations) to drive ADR/mix. Priority 2: Debt servicing (currently comfortable at INR 264cr). Priority 3: Greenfield development (Madhapur). Dividends: Management targets resumption by FY27 end post-convention center completion and stabilization.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Geopolitical tensions impacting travel sentiment (noted in March '26 softness). 2) Execution risk on renovation timelines delaying ADR upside. 3) Interest rate sensitivity on INR 264cr debt. 4) Potential supply surge in Hyderabad by FY30-31 (though management sees delays in competitor projects). 5) Customer mix cyclicality (group vs transient) during convention center downtime.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; acknowledges near-term geopolitical headwinds but emphasizes structural demand and supply scarcity. Transparent on debt increase for MEA acquisition and PAT distortion due to prior year tax adjustments. Aggressive on ADR targets (25-30% total growth potential) and cost rationalization.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 1) 65% of current occupancy comes from Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, reducing OTA commission drag (targeting 80-85%). 2) Legacy management contracts signed in 2006/2008 provide favorable terms vs new market entrants. 3) Courtyard occupancy dip to 52% in FY26 was entirely renovation-driven and has already normalized to ~95-99% for new inventory. 4) MEA segment has virtually no new supply pipeline in Hyderabad, creating a moat for extended-stay pricing.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Investment strategy focuses on three criteria: greenfield developments, brownfield operational enhancements, and NCLT distressed asset turnarounds, all evaluated for financial viability, location feasibility, and unique value proposition.
- Balance sheet shows long-term borrowings of ₹24,539.5 lakhs as of March 2026, reflecting debt-funded expansion and acquisition activity.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Hotels (Marriott/Courtyard): Room rev 55-60%, F&B 35-40%; F&B margins 45-50%. Extended Stay (MEA): Room rev 64-65%, F&B 32-33%; Higher EBITDA contribution due to limited F&B overhead. MEA Q4 Rev: INR 12.7cr (Room INR 9cr + F&B INR 3.7cr). Seasonality: Q3/Q4 occupancy 80%+ (peaking 90%); Q1/Q2 ~70%.

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply scarcity in Hyderabad premium segment combined with Viceroy's aggressive renovation-driven ADR uplift (targeting 25-30% growth) positions them to outperform peers facing flat pricing. | Viceroy Hotels Limited | beneficiary | High | Consolidation of high-margin MEA assets and imminent completion of convention center renovations create a visible earnings inflection point for FY27, while debt levels are deemed manageable post-acquisition. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Operates 463 rooms across three operational Marriott-branded properties in Hyderabad (Marriott Hyderabad, Courtyard by Marriott, Marriott Executive Apartments), targeting corporate, MICE, and long-stay expatriate segments.
- Properties are strategically located near Hyderabad's key business hubs (HITEC City, Gachibowli, Financial District) and convention venues, with proximity to airports and tourist attractions.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: - [Resolution Plan Exit] The company emerged from CIRP under the Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code in 2023, with Anirudh Agro Farms Limited (via SPV Loko Hospitality) executing the resolution plan, including a ₹60 crore equity infusion and restructuring of public shareholding.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded 183bps QoQ to 31.4% driven by high-margin MEA consolidation and Phase 1 renovation efficiencies. Cost saves: Laundry outsourced (cost down 35-40%), HVAC upgrades reducing power costs, shared back-office functions across 3 properties. F&B gross margin ~85%, operating margin 45-50%.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue: Double-digit growth expected FY27 (organic 5-7% + renovation driven); Margin: EBITDA to expand via convention center completion (targeting 2x EBITDA from MICE) and backend efficiencies; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: Convention center renovation completes FY27 (1.5yr payback); Phase 2 (Marriott) completes FY27; Phase 3 completes FY28; Madhapur greenfield opens FY29-30.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A - Service sector; however, renovation pipeline includes INR 100cr+ committed capex across 3 phases with Phase 1 (Courtyard) complete, Phase 2 (Marriott) underway (Apr '26 start), and Phase 3 targeted for FY28.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) Convention Center expansion (20k sq ft) expected to double MICE EBITDA upon FY27 completion. 2) Madhapur greenfield project (pure room play, high GOP) targeting FY29/30 opening in supply-scarce IT corridor. 3) Distressed asset acquisitions (NCLT) under evaluation, though deal flow currently thin due to sector strength. 4) ADR upside: Targeting INR 9,000-9,500 short-term (vs current ~INR 7,600) and INR 10,000 long-term via refurbishment (20-22% uplift) + organic growth (5-7%).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Viceroy Hotels delivered a 35.3% Q4 revenue surge driven by the consolidation of Marriott Executive Apartments, masking a softer underlying organic trend due to geopolitical headwinds. The core investment thesis hinges on a INR 100cr+ renovation program already driving 20-22% ADR uplifts in renovated inventory, with FY27 poised for margin expansion as convention center upgrades complete and debt stabilizes post-acquisition.

open.item: Phase 2 renovation at Marriott Hyderabad commenced in April 2026 and is expected to be completed during FY27.
Marriott Hyderabad Convention Center renovation started in April 2026 and is expected to finish by end of FY27.
Courtyard by Marriott occupancy, which dipped to 52.2% in FY26 due to renovation, is expected to normalize in FY27.
Year-on-year revenue growth expected to be double-digit going forward, though Q4 jump was partly due to MEA consolidation.
Expanded 20,000 sq ft Marriott convention centre renovation (started first week April 2026) to be finished by end of this year, with investment recouped in about one and a half years.
Intend to increase F&B share and profitability until FY28 as the convention centre returns and rooms are upgraded; F&B margin ~45-50% with gross margin ~85%.
Phase 3 renovation is targeted for completion during FY28.
Board has discussed dividends; management expects to give a good outcome from next year (FY28).
Management expects to give a good outcome on dividends from next year, after the convention centre renovation completes by end of this year.
Investment in Marriott Convention Center renovation expected to be recouped in 1.5 years.
Courtyard by Marriott Madhapur (Hyderabad IT corridor) is targeted to open in FY29 or FY30.
Adding the new convention centre plus renovating the old one expected to drive a substantial twofold increase in EBITDA, with three-property integration improving GOPs.
Flagged softer Q4/March operating environment from West Asia conflict and inflation, but sees little new Hyderabad supply for the next couple of years supporting ADRs.
Total phased investment and renovation program across hospitality portfolio is over INR 100 crores.
Portfolio occupancy is expected to be ~70% in Q1-Q2 and 80%+ in Q3-Q4.
Combined RevPAR declined slightly in FY26; management is implementing dynamic pricing, weekend packages, spa, rooftop restaurant to drive RevPAR growth.
Management is comfortable with current debt levels and does not anticipate further increases in interest expense; healthy cash flows to fund ongoing renovations.
Company continues to evaluate greenfield and brownfield development opportunities along with select distressed assets (NCLT) for long-term growth.
Target to increase Marriott Bonvoy direct channel contribution from current ~65% to 80-85% to reduce OTA commissions.
Expect ADR growth of ~5-7% organic plus 20-22% from refurbishment, combining to roughly 25-30% ADR growth as new inventory comes in.

revisions.item: From the existing complex, management expects a 30% to 40% increase in revenue as renovation completes.
Expect annual revenue to grow at least 30-35% once the entire renovation is completed, with F&B/banqueting staying at 45-48% of revenue.
Year-on-year revenue growth expected to be double-digit going forward, though Q4 jump was partly due to MEA consolidation.
Management expects organic ADR growth of 5-7% annually, plus 20-22% from refurbishment, targeting combined ADR of INR 9,000-9,500 near-term and ~10,000 long-term for Marriott and Courtyard complex.

verdicts.item: Management expects ADRs to improve to the INR9,500-INR10,500 mark once the renovation is complete.
verdicts.note: ADR target reaffirmed (aim 9,000-9,500 immediate, 10,000 long-run); current ~7,605, not yet at 9,500-10,500.

verdicts.item: EBITDA margin, now near 30%, expected to breach and be sustained above 30% once renovation completes and ADRs improve.
verdicts.note: Q4 margin breached 30% at 31.4% (FY26 29.8%); renovation ongoing so not yet 'sustained' above 30%. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: New Courtyard rooms to be marketed as premium club-level rooms with ADR 25-30% higher than the rest of the inventory.
verdicts.note: New premier rooms selling near-full; premium positioning confirmed, but explicit 25-30% ADR premium not restated. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: For the following financial year (FY27) management targets 5-7% growth amid ongoing phased renovation, while aspiring to beat the ~7% industry at ~10%.
168 of the 295 Marriott rooms to be refurbished (20-30 at a time) by end of next year, i.e. up to 31 March 2027.
verdicts.note: Marriott rooms being upgraded, continuing over next two financial years; Phase 2 completion FY27 (aligns with Mar-2027 target).

verdicts.item: Phase 2 Convention Center to be taken out on 1 April 2026 and completed in six months, by 30 September 2026.
verdicts.note: Convention centre started April 2026 but completion now year-end/FY27, later than the promised 30 Sep 2026.

verdicts.item: Total three-phase budget ~INR120 crores, ~INR50 crores spent (Courtyard done); balance ~INR70 crores to be spent at Marriott on rooms, convention centre and F&B.
verdicts.note: Three-phase ~100cr+ program: Courtyard/Phase 1 complete, balance being spent at Marriott.

verdicts.item: Portfolio-level EBITDA margin targeted north of 30%, with a longer-term aim of reaching the 40% mark once all 463 rooms and the modern convention centre are upgraded.
verdicts.note: Near-term >30% margin achieved in Q4 (31.4%); 40% long-term goal pending full 463-room + convention upgrade. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: All 168 rooms of Courtyard expected operational by November 30, coinciding with the strongest two quarters.
verdicts.note: Phase 1 complete, Courtyard renovation dip 'back to normal'; new rooms near-full occupancy. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Phase 1 at Courtyard (spa, gym, bar) to be finished by end of December, with the phase completed by end of Q3 FY26.
verdicts.note: 'first phase relating to Courtyard by Marriott Hyderabad has now been completed successfully.'

verdicts.item: Phase 2 to upgrade 168 rooms of Marriott and expand the Convention Center; Phase 3 covers F&B outlets, executive lounge, lobby and 127 additional guest rooms.
verdicts.note: Phase 2 (rooms + convention) commenced April 2026; Phase 3 F&B/lobby/rooms targeted FY28. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Actively evaluating inorganic/brownfield and distressed assets across Tier I cities including Bangalore, Goa, Pune and Chandigarh.
verdicts.note: Continues evaluating NCLT/distressed assets ('nothing materialized yet'); completed MEA acquisition.

wtt.summary: 25% guidance hit (4 chains); 2/2 projects on-time; 4 guidance revision(s); 16% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and optimistic; management acknowledged softer Q4 due to geopolitical tensions but emphasized resilient performance, renovation progress, and strong long-term outlook. No explicit misses owned, but Courtyard occupancy dip was attributed to renovation and said to be normalizing.
